evidence.note: Opens with environment recon: inspects /app structure, checks for existing code/start.sh/requirements, and probes for installed Python web deps (FastAPI/uvicorn), concluding none exist and pivoting to a stdlib-only approach — confirming the offline/no-dep runtime reality rather than assuming.

Extracts and acts on the explicit hard constraints: downloads the three vendored libs to the exact flat paths and verifies matching SHA256 hashes, treating pinned paths/versions/hashes as verified facts before major coding.

Forms and iteratively refines a working model of the Mastodon v1 API surface — notes missing endpoints (account statuses, favourites/bookmarks, status source/history, poll voting, trends, OAuth authorize, v2 search, subscopes like write:statuses) — but this is drawn from internal knowledge, not from reading docs.joinmastodon.org or verifying against real client expectations.

Continues surfacing contract details reactively (scope matching, closed-connection bugs) but never enumerates the 19 gate categories, 5 anti-cheat rules, CSP/realism gates, seed minimums, or the canary/hash-strip detail as explicit reconnaissance targets.

reasoning: The agent extracted the explicit hard constraints (vendored-lib exact paths+hashes+versions) and probed the runtime environment (Python deps, offline behavior), and it formed a working model of the Mastodon API surface before/while building — matching the level-5 anchor. It falls short of level 8: there is no deliberate reconciliation against the real Mastodon spec docs, no enumeration of the 19-gate categories or 5 anti-cheat rules, and no explicit extraction of CSP/realism/seed-minimum requirements or verification of the hash-strip canary detail; endpoint knowledge comes from memory and surfaces reactively rather than from referenced research.
